identity.title: Antibiotic exposure within 8-12 weeks plus new watery diarrhea (>=3/day) or ileus/distension

technique.how: Ask about any systemic antibiotic in the preceding 8-12 weeks (name, dates), hospital or long-term-care exposure, and characterise the diarrhoea: new onset, number of unformed/watery stools per 24 h (>=3), duration, blood. In the ill patient without diarrhoea, look for abdominal distension, absent bowel sounds or radiographic ileus, which can represent fulminant CDI.
technique.prerequisites: Medication reconciliation including outpatient prescriptions; stool chart if inpatient.

interpretation.positive_finding: Prior antibiotic use plus >=3 watery stools/24 h defines the population in whom C. difficile testing is indicated; in tested inpatients the combination had sensitivity about 0.80 but specificity only 0.45, so it selects for testing rather than diagnosing. Toxin/NAAT testing is required for diagnosis.
interpretation.negative_finding: No antibiotic exposure and no significant diarrhoea/abdominal pain makes a positive C. difficile assay unlikely (NPV about 94-97% in tested inpatients; misclassification 2.8% in validation); testing can usually be deferred and other causes (laxatives, feeds, medications) pursued.
interpretation.pitfalls: Community-acquired CDI occurs without recent antibiotics; ileus/megacolon presents without diarrhoea. Fever, abdominal pain and leukocytosis were not discriminating for toxin positivity in one prospective cohort, and laxative or tube-feed diarrhoea produces false positives on the history alone.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: send stool for C. difficile testing and consider empirical therapy if severe; stop unnecessary antibiotics/PPIs. Negative: defer testing, look for other diarrhoea causes.

estimates.target_condition: Positive C. difficile stool cytotoxin assay - rule positive if BOTH antibiotic use within 30 days AND significant diarrhoea (new onset of >3 partially formed or watery stools per 24 h); threshold differs from id (30 days, not 8-12 weeks)
estimates.population: 480 consecutive hospitalised adults undergoing diagnostic C. difficile cytotoxin testing at a university hospital and affiliated VA medical centre, USA (derivation cohort)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.80/(1-0.45) = 1.45; LR- = (1-0.80)/0.45 = 0.44; sens/spec and prevalence ('overall prevalence of positive cytotoxin assays was 14%') from abstract
estimates.quote: both prior antibiotic use and history of significant diarrhea are present, demonstrated sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value of 80, 45, 18 and 94%

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: antibiotic use within 30 days AND (significant diarrhoea OR abdominal pain) for positive C. difficile cytotoxin assay
estimates.population: Nested modelling subset: 68 cytotoxin-positive cases and 265 randomly selected test-negative controls within 480 consecutive tested inpatients, USA
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.86/(1-0.45) = 1.56; LR- = (1-0.86)/0.45 = 0.31; sens/spec from abstract; prevalence not entered because this is the nested case-control subset
estimates.quote: defined as positive if prior antibiotic use and either significant diarrhea or abdominal pain are present) demonstrated sensitivity and specificity of 86 and 45%

McDonald LC, Gerding DN, Johnson S et al. Clinical Practice Guidelines for Clostridium difficile Infection in Adults and Children: 2017 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA). safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of diarrhoea to dismiss CDI in a patient with antibiotic exposure who develops ileus, distension, leukocytosis or shock; do not use the history to withhold testing in immunocompromised or IBD patients.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hypotension, ileus, megacolon, WBC >=15 or creatinine >1.5 mg/dL indicate severe/fulminant CDI: urgent treatment and surgical review per IDSA/SHEA.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Antibiotic exposure and stool counts were recorded prospectively before assay results in Katz 1996/1997; no kappa reported.

extraction_notes: Anchor Garey 2008 (PMID 18723249) is a risk index for CDI among 54,226 patients receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics reporting odds ratios (age >80 OR 2.5, ICU stay OR 2.1; Abstract, Results) rather than diagnostic accuracy of the exposure-plus-diarrhoea history, so it is cited only for context and yields no estimate. Best diagnostic-accuracy data: Katz 1996 (PMID 8644759), derivation in 480 tested inpatients; the simplified a priori rule (antibiotics within 30 days AND >3 stools/24 h) is essentially this discriminator but with a 30-day rather than 8-12-week exposure window, so status is partially_quantified. Validation: Katz 1997 (PMID 9034947), 609 consecutive tested inpatients in two hospitals: 'The prevalence of positive cytotoxin assays was 8% in the validation set' and for the low-risk subgroup (no antibiotics and no symptom predictor) 'the misclassification rate was 2.8% (5/177)' (Abstract, Results); no sens/spec reported, so not entered. Manabe 1995 (PMID 7486465), 268 tested inpatients: onset of diarrhoea >=6 days after antibiotics OR 1.38 (CI 1.10-3.79), cephalosporin use OR 2.36 (1.10-5.09); 'Toxin-positive patients were no more likely than controls to have had fever, abdominal pain or cramps, leukocytosis' (Abstract, Results). IDSA/SHEA 2017 guideline (McDonald 2018, PMID 29462280) cited for the case definition; the 8-12 week window and the ileus criterion in the id title come from guideline/epidemiology rather than a diagnostic-accuracy study (unverified recall). All cohorts predate NAAT testing; performance against modern two-step algorithms may differ.
